Bring your [Unmanic](https://docs.unmanic.app) server (the self-hosted video
library optimizer) into Gladys, over your local network: the tasks waiting and
in progress, the tasks completed and failed today, the state and progress of
each worker, pause switches, and scenes that react when a task fails or when
the queue is empty.

The integration was tested against a real Unmanic 0.4.1 server (the official
`josh5/unmanic` Docker image, with real transcode tasks and a failed one), not
yet in a real Gladys installation: feedback is welcome on the
[Gladys forum](https://community.gladysassistant.com) or in the
[issues](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-unmanic/issues).

## What you need

- Gladys Assistant 5.1.0 or later.
- An **Unmanic** server reachable from Gladys (same network), on the port of
  its web interface (`8888` by default).
- Unmanic has **no login of its own**: nothing to create. If you put a reverse
  proxy with Basic auth in front of it, keep its user name and password at
  hand.

## Set up

1. Install the integration from the Gladys catalog.
2. In **Configuration**, enter the **Address** of the Unmanic server (for
   example `192.168.1.2:8888`; without a port, `8888` is used). Behind a
   reverse proxy, the full address (`https://example.org/unmanic`) and, with
   Basic auth, the **User name (reverse proxy)** and **Password (reverse
   proxy)**.
3. Save, then click **Test the connection**: the message under the button gives
   the version of Unmanic, the number of workers and the tasks waiting.
4. Open the **Discover** tab: one device for the server, one for the queue, one
   per worker. Click **Add** on the ones you want, pick a room and save.

Options:

- **Allow pause and resume** (off by default): Gladys may pause and resume the
  workers (switches, scenes, widget button). Off, the integration only reads.
- **Refresh interval**: 30 seconds to 5 minutes (1 minute by default).
- **Language of the feature names**: the names given to the features when a
  device is added, and the language of the summary sentence.

## The devices

**The Unmanic server**

| Feature                | What it shows                                               |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Online**             | 1 while the server answers.                                 |
| **All workers paused** | Switch: pauses or resumes every worker (1 when all paused). |
| **Version**            | Version of Unmanic.                                         |

**The Unmanic queue**

| Feature               | What it shows                                              |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Waiting tasks**     | Tasks waiting for a worker (the Pending tasks of Unmanic). |
| **Tasks in progress** | Tasks a worker is processing right now.                    |
| **Completed today**   | Tasks completed with success since midnight.               |
| **Failed today**      | Tasks failed since midnight.                               |

**Each worker** (named after the worker in Unmanic, `Default-Worker-1`…)

| Feature              | What it shows                                                     |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Active**           | 1 while the worker processes a task.                              |
| **Paused**           | Switch: pauses or resumes this worker.                            |
| **Progress**         | Progress of the task in %, when the plugin of Unmanic reports it. |
| **File in progress** | Name of the file being processed (`—` when idle).                 |

A paused worker stops its task where it is and goes on from there when it is
resumed: nothing is lost. A worker that disappears (worker group shrunk or
renamed in Unmanic) stays in Gladys, offline.

## Dashboard

The **Unmanic** widget shows four tiles (waiting, in progress, done today,
failed today), one row per worker (progress and file, paused, idle) and a
button: **Pause all** while the workers run, **Resume all** once they are all
paused. No button when the commands are off in the configuration. Two settings
of the widget hide the worker rows and the button.

## Scenes

### Triggers

- **Unmanic queue emptied**: everything is processed, no task waiting and no
  worker busy any more. Variables: the tasks completed and failed today.
- **Unmanic task failed**: a task has just ended in failure. Variables: the
  file name, the tasks failed today.

### Actions

- **Pause Unmanic**: one worker, or every worker when no worker is chosen.
- **Resume Unmanic**: same choice.
- **Read the Unmanic summary**: a sentence for a message or a voice
  announcement ("Unmanic: 12 task(s) waiting, 2 in progress, 30 completed
  today, 1 failed today."), and the same figures as numbers.

The pause and resume actions need **Allow pause and resume** in the
configuration.

### Scene ideas

- During the peak hours of your electricity contract, **Pause Unmanic**; when
  the off-peak hours start, **Resume Unmanic**.
- **Unmanic task failed** → send a Telegram message with the file name.
- **Unmanic queue emptied** → a notification: "Unmanic is done for today".
- In the evening, **Pause Unmanic** to keep the CPU for the movie, and resume
  it at night.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Unmanic does not answer"**: check the address and the port (`8888`), and
  that Gladys reaches the server (firewall, Docker network).
- **"Access refused"**: a reverse proxy protects Unmanic; check the user name
  and password in the configuration.
- **"No Unmanic server at this address"**: another application answers on this
  port, or the base path of the reverse proxy is missing.
- **No worker**: Unmanic has no worker until a worker group has one
  (**Settings** → **Workers**).
- **The progress stays at 0 %**: the plugin of the task gives Unmanic no
  progress; the worker is still shown active with its file.
- **The switch does nothing**: check **Allow pause and resume** in the
  configuration.
- More details in the logs of the integration (**Integrations** → Unmanic →
  logs), at the `debug` level if needed.

## Limits

- One Unmanic server per integration.
- The figures are read every refresh interval: a short task may start and end
  between two readings (it is still counted in the tasks of the day).
- The tasks of the day are counted from the 250 latest tasks of the history,
  from midnight in the time zone of Gladys. **Unmanic task failed** announces
  at most ten tasks per reading, none older than an hour.
- Unmanic has no authentication: anyone on your network reaches its API. The
  integration does not change the settings, libraries or plugins of Unmanic,
  and deletes nothing.
- Not affiliated with Unmanic or its authors.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Unmanic asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unmanic server | `section` | No | Address of the Unmanic web interface. Unmanic has no login of its own: fill in the user name and password only if a reverse proxy with Basic auth protects it. |
| Address | `string` | No | IP address or name of the server, with the port of the web interface (8888 by default). |
| User name (reverse proxy) | `string` | No | Only behind a reverse proxy with Basic auth. Leave empty otherwise. |
| Password (reverse proxy) | `secret` | No | Password of the reverse proxy, with the user name above. |
| Allow pause and resume | `boolean` | No | Gladys may pause and resume the workers (switches, scenes, widget button). Off: read only. |
| Refresh interval | `select` | No | How often the server is read: queue, workers, completed tasks. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Names given to the features when a device is added, and the sentence of the summary action. |

## How to install Unmanic in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Unmanic appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-unmanic:1.0.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-unmanic](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-unmanic).

Unmanic requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Unmanic is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [guim31](https://github.com/guim31), not by the Gladys core team.
